details: Annual US inflation, as measured by the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, held steady at 3.7% in July, remaining above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for the 65th consecutive month. This persistence, exacerbated by spiraling energy prices following US and Israeli attacks on Iran, intensifies the debate within the Federal Reserve on whether to raise interest rates or hold them steady. Economists had projected a slightly lower PCE reading of 3.6%.
title: US Inflation Sticky, Debate Over Rate Hikes Intensifies

details: Bitcoin touched a more than three-month high, surpassing $80,000, after the US Treasury announced an expansion of its long-dated bond buyback operations. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed that the Treasury would continue debt auctions despite increasing buyback sizes for 10- to 30-year securities, aiming to cap long-end yields. This move has been interpreted by analysts as providing relief from high bond yields and a "soft dollar," contributing to a significant boost in the cryptocurrency sector.
title: Bitcoin Surges as Treasury Expands Bond Buybacks

details: Iran is emphasizing self-sufficiency as it navigates an ongoing economic confrontation with the United States. This stance comes as the US maintains and expands economic pressure, including sanctions, on nations like Iran. Such geopolitical tensions can create uncertainty in global markets and potentially impact oil prices and international trade, indirectly affecting broader financial stability.
title: Iran Stresses Self-Sufficiency Amidst US Economic War
